content: Using the applicator provided, insert one vaginal tablet into the vagina once daily for two weeks. This applies to both adults and adolescents. Do not use this medication in combination with other vaginal products, as this may interfere with the release of progesterone. The use of nystatin vaginal tablets or progesterone intravaginal gel is contraindicated in certain cases. If irritation or sensitization occurs during use, discontinue treatment immediately and inform the patient about the symptoms of irritation or sensitization. Patients should be advised not to interrupt or discontinue the medication, even during menstruation, as symptomatic relief may occur within a few days. Cleansing douches may be used by non-pregnant women for aesthetic purposes if desired. There is no evidence that the use of nystatin vaginal inserts during pregnancy increases the risk of fetal abnormalities or affects the child’s growth, development, or functional maturation. However, due to the possibility of harm, nystatin vaginal inserts should only be used during pregnancy if deemed essential by the physician. Caution is advised as there is no data available on excretion into human breast milk. Nystatin is an antifungal agent that binds to sterols in the fungal cell membrane, causing changes in permeability and leakage of intracellular contents. Systemic absorption is unlikely, as it is poorly absorbed through intact skin and mucous membranes. For topical use, nystatin is used to treat fungal skin infections. Clean and thoroughly dry the affected area before application. Apply the medication to the affected skin as directed by your doctor, usually two or three times daily. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on the type of infection being treated. Apply enough powder to lightly coat the affected area and some surrounding skin. Wash your hands after application unless treating the hands. Do not wrap, cover, or bandage the area unless instructed by your doctor. Use the medication regularly to achieve the best results and continue until the full prescribed amount is finished, even if symptoms disappear after a few days. Common side effects may include skin irritation or redness. Serious allergic reactions are rare. If you experience severe symptoms, such as passing out or difficulty breathing, seek emergency medical attention immediately. For non-emergencies, contact a poison control center. In the U.S., call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Before using nystatin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Store the medication at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
